# A16 scope: class trends alongside each grading tool, generated by a run

Seat: SCOPING. Authored 2026-09-20 against the working tree at `main` (dirty:
`git status --short` shows 17 modified files, all under
`src/app/components/snapshot-grading/`, `src/app/components/assessment-shared/`,
`src/lib/grade/prompts.ts`, `src/tools/backlog/`, plus `docs/BACKLOG.md` and
`docs/backlog.yml` - i.e. the live work I was told to avoid).

Owner's words, which define done:

> "this thing needs to live alongside each of the grading tools in the tools
> tab. when i run a tool over a series of assignments, that run should generate
> trends"

> "moving that is top priority"

## 0. The three findings that change the item

Read these before section 1; the rest of this document is their evidence.

**F1. The Recording strip's two grading tools cannot feed class trends today,
and one of them cannot without a data change in a directory that is under live
edit.** `computeClassTrends` reads `result.rubricAreas[].area` and
`.score` (`src/lib/grade/class-trends.ts:288,303`). The snapshot tool's row
carries exactly that (`SnapshotAssessmentRow.rubricAreas: SnapshotRubricAreaEvidence[]`,
`src/app/components/snapshot-grading/snapshot-row.ts:122,124`, with `area: string`
and `score: string` at `:90,91`). The recording tool's row does **not**:
`composeGradingRowResult` parses `rubricAreas` and then **discards them**,
returning only four strings (`src/app/components/grading-recording/grading-feedback-prompt.ts:146-155`,
returning `GradingRecordingFeedback` declared at `:47-58` as
`totalScore/strengths/improvements/overallComment/failed`). Mounting today's
panel against that surface renders `Trends (0)` forever. Retaining the areas
means editing `grading-feedback-prompt.ts` - inside
`src/app/components/grading-recording/`, which I was told to avoid.

**F2. No grading surface in this tree runs over a series of ASSIGNMENTS except
the workflow grading step - and its consumer is the one place trends already
lives.** `GradingRunEntry` is one assignment (`src/lib/grade/types.ts:329-338`,
doc comment at `:320-321`: "One assignment's grading run"). The only arrays of
it are `GradingDraftPayload.runs: GradingRunEntry[]`
(`src/lib/grading-drafts.ts:32-33`) and the workflow step's own
`const runs: GradingRunEntry[]` built by looping `for (const row of plan)`
over assignments (`src/lib/workflows/registry/steps.grading-run.ts:425,428,496`).
DraftedGradesTab renders a draft's `runs` as groups
(`src/app/components/DraftedGradesTab.tsx:606`) and mounts trends **per group**
(`:627`). So the series already exists at the existing site and the existing
panel deliberately does not span it.

**F3. Trends is already in the Tools tab.** `manual: "Tools"` at
`src/app/components/tabs/tab-sections.ts:40` (the tab value is `"manual"`, the
label is "Tools"; that file's `:22` comment says so explicitly). The Tools tab's
rail is ten chips - seven Manual views (`MANUAL_VIEW_ORDER`,
`src/app/components/manual/manual-rail.ts:110-118`) plus three Workflows views -
built at `src/app/components/tabs/tab-rails.ts:132-149`. DraftedGradesTab is the
Workflows > Drafts > Grades chip (`src/app/components/home/WorkflowsPanel.tsx:77`).
The owner's "in the tools tab" is therefore not a tab move; it is "alongside the
grading tools" **within** a tab it is already in.

### 1d. Per grading tool: does a run carry enough identity to be a series?

This is the section the item turns on. "Series" is read two ways below because
the owner's sentence is ambiguous and the answer differs: **series-of-students**
(one assignment, N submissions - what layer A computes today) versus
**series-of-assignments** (N assignments - what the owner literally wrote).

| Grading surface | Where | Run object today | Series of students? | Series of assignments? | Per-area scores on the row? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Grading (from a recording) | `RecordingTab.tsx:857`, `GradingRecordingPanel` | **None.** Per-row dispatch into a persisted table (`STORAGE_KEY_TABLE = "ta-rec-grade-table"`, `useGradingRows.ts:184`) | Only as an accumulating table, no run boundary | No | **NO** - discarded at `grading-feedback-prompt.ts:148-155` |
| Grading (from screenshots) | `RecordingTab.tsx:867`, `SnapshotGradingPanel` | **None.** Same shape: `ta-snap-table` (`grep -o 'ta-[a-z-]*' src/app/components/snapshot-grading/*.ts \| sort -u`) | Only as an accumulating table | No | **YES** - `snapshot-row.ts:122-124` |
| LMS > Grading, zip mode (assignment upload) | `GradingTab.tsx:26` `GradingMode="zip"`, results at `:427` | `GradeActionState.run: GradingRun \| null` (`src/app/actions-types.ts:80-85`) | **YES** - one submit, N students | No - one assignment per submit | **YES** - `GradeResult.rubricAreas` |
| LMS > Grading, canvas mode | same | same | YES | No | YES |
| LMS > Grading, livefeed mode | `GradingTab.tsx:211` -> `LiveFeedPanel.tsx:430` | same `GradingRun` | YES | No | YES |
| LMS > Grading, github mode | `GradingTab.tsx:209` -> `GithubGradingPanel.tsx:852` | same `GradingRun` | YES | No | YES |
| Repo Grades | `manualView === "repo-grades"`, `src/app/components/repo-grades/index.tsx` | Bulk grade is scoped to ONE folder (`setRunningFolder(folder)`, `useRepoGradesBulkGrade.ts:177-178`) | YES per folder | **The GRID does** - `RepoGradeCellEditsByRepo = Record<repo, Record<assignment, RepoGradeCellEdit>>` (`repoGradesCellEdits.ts:200`) - but no single run spans it | **YES** - `rubricAreas: RubricAreaResult[]`, `repoGradesCellEdits.ts:102` |
| Files > Submissions, cartridge drop | `FilesTab.tsx:852`, `CartridgeDropPanel` (544 lines) | its own path | YES | No | via `GradingRun` |
| Workflows > grade steps (unattended) | `steps.grading-run.ts:425-496`, `steps.grading-repos.ts`, `steps.grading-draft-flow.ts`, `steps.grading-cartridge.ts` | **`runs: GradingRunEntry[]`** | YES | **YES - the only one** | YES |
| Workflows > Drafts > Grades | `DraftedGradesTab.tsx`, consuming `GradingDraftPayload.runs` | `runs: GradingRunEntry[]` | YES | **YES** (a draft holds several) | YES |

**So, stated plainly:** the owner's literal ask - a run over a series of
assignments generating trends - is satisfiable TODAY by exactly one producer
(the workflow grade step) and is already displayed, per-assignment-not-per-series,
by exactly one consumer (Drafted Grades). Every interactive grading tool in the
Tools tab runs one assignment at a time. **Nothing needs a run identity
invented for the series-of-students reading; a run identity would have to be
invented for the series-of-assignments reading on every interactive tool.**

## 2. The two halves, sized separately

### Half 1: PLACEMENT - small, and smaller than it looks

The panel's only real dependency is `{ run, assignmentName }` (section 1b).
`GradingResults.tsx` already receives `run: GradingRun` and `canvasUrl: string`
(`GradingResults.tsx:91-94`) and is the **shared** results renderer for three of
the four LMS grading modes: `GradingTab.tsx:427`, `GithubGradingPanel.tsx:852`,
`LiveFeedPanel.tsx:430`. One mount there reaches three surfaces.

Size: widen the panel's prop from `entry` to `{ run, assignmentName }` (three
call sites inside the panel), add one mount in `GradingResults.tsx`, update the
wiring test's `entry={entry}` pin. Roughly 40-60 lines of diff.

The constraint is not complexity, it is **line budget**. Measured with
`@(Get-Content <f>).Count` against the 1000-line repo-wide ceiling
(`src/file-size-ceiling.structure.test.ts:30`, `LIMIT = 1000`; the
`ALLOWED_OVERAGE` table at `:64-81` contains none of these files, so the hard
1000 applies):

| File | Lines | Headroom |
|---|---|---|
| `src/app/components/grading-recording/GradingRecordingPanel.tsx` | **995** | **5** |
| `src/app/components/snapshot-grading/SnapshotGradingPanel.tsx` | **970** | 30 |
| `src/app/components/RecordingTab.tsx` | 917 | 83 |
| `src/app/components/GradingResults.tsx` | 916 | 84 |
| `src/app/components/repo-grades/index.tsx` | 913 | 87 |
| `src/app/components/GithubGradingPanel.tsx` | 889 | 111 |
| `src/app/components/DraftedGradesTab.tsx` | 870 | 130 |
| `src/app/components/LiveFeedPanel.tsx` | 709 | 291 |
| `src/app/components/GradingTab.tsx` | 460 | 540 |

`this-repo.md` records `GradingRecordingPanel.tsx` at 964; it is **995** today.
Re-measured, not recalled.

### Half 2: TRIGGER - the substantive half, and its mechanism

The owner's word is "generate", against a current UI where trends is **two
clicks behind a collapsed button**: `ClassTrendsPanel.tsx:124` renders
`Trends (N)` / `Hide trends` and the whole body is behind `expanded &&` at
`:127`. Layer A is already computed on every render
(`useMemo(() => computeClassTrends(entry), [entry])`, `:80`) - it is the
DISCLOSURE, not the computation, that is gated.

**Mechanism, concretely, and it is three separate decisions - do not collapse
them:**

1. **Layer A becomes an output of the run, not a destination.** Render the
   counted per-area list expanded by default whenever the run has at least one
   graded result, instead of behind the `expanded` toggle. This costs no network
   call, no model call, no storage: `computeClassTrends` is pure
   (`class-trends.ts:250-258` header states it). This is the whole of "that run
   should generate trends" for layer A and it is essentially free.
   - Per the repo's persisted-control rule, if the toggle survives at all its
     state must persist under a `ta-` key; if it is replaced by default-open,
     nothing new persists. **Recommend default-open with a collapse control
     whose state persists**, because a default-open panel that the instructor
     cannot quiet is a regression for a 30-student table.

2. **Layer B (the model reading) stays explicitly opt-in.** It is a 50-second
   budgeted model call (`route.ts:47-51`) behind `requireUser()` (`:22`).
   Firing it automatically on every run turns every grading pass into a paid
   model call the instructor did not ask for. **Recommend: unchanged.** If the
   owner wants it automatic, that is their call to overrule and it should be
   recorded as one.

3. **Layer C (the student-facing draft) stays opt-in and keeps its floor
   question with N13a.** Unchanged by A16.

**What half 2 does NOT require:** a run identity, a run id, or any new
persistence, *under the series-of-students reading*. Under the
series-of-assignments reading it requires, per tool, either a grouping key the
tool does not have (recording/snapshot grading: no run object at all, section
1d) or a cross-run accumulator that does not exist anywhere outside
`GradingDraftPayload.runs`. **I did not find a cheap version of the
series-of-assignments reading for any interactive tool, and I am not proposing
one.** See residual RES-A16-1 and the batched owner question in section 8.

## 4. Move or fan out

**Recommendation: FAN OUT. Do not move, do not delete the DraftedGradesTab
site.**

Reasons, in order of weight:

1. **They answer different questions and the existing one answers the harder
   one.** DraftedGradesTab renders trends **per entry inside a draft that holds
   several entries** (`DraftedGradesTab.tsx:606`, over
   `GradingDraftPayload.runs`, `grading-drafts.ts:33`). That is the only place in
   the app where an instructor sees several assignments' trends side by side.
   A run-generated panel on `GradingResults` answers "what did the batch I just
   graded have in common"; the drafts panel answers "what did this week of
   grading look like". Deleting the second to satisfy "move it" loses the only
   thing in the tree that is close to the owner's literal "series of
   assignments".

2. **Deleting it deletes shipped, baselined behaviour.** `docs/REGRESSION.md`
   entry 422 (`grep -an "class trends" docs/REGRESSION.md` -> line 42824,
   "N12: the class-trends feature becomes reachable") records this exact mount
   as the fix for a feature that had shipped dead. Entry 423 covers layer C.
   Moving the mount silently re-opens the question entry 422 closed.

3. **The panel is cheap to mount twice.** It is pure until the instructor asks
   for layer B (`class-trends.ts` header `:4-15`), so a second mount costs one
   `useMemo` per run on screen.

**What the owner is overruling if they say "move it":** they are deciding that
the per-draft, multi-assignment review view is not worth keeping, and that the
Drafted Grades group header loses its trends button. That is a legitimate call -
it reduces two surfaces to one and the drafts view may be one they never use -
but it must be a stated decision, because it is a capability deletion and
`docs/REGRESSION.md` entry 422 will need amending in the same commit. **I am
not recommending it and I would not do it without the owner saying the word
"delete".**

## 5. The shape: strip entries versus a panel inside each tool

**Recommendation: a panel INSIDE the existing surfaces. No new strip entry.**

### Weighing the hardcoded strip counts

`src/app/components/recording/recording-split.structure.test.ts` (590 lines)
holds four assertions over the strip. Verified by opening the file:

| Assertion | Line | Current value | What a 13th entry does |
|---|---|---|---|
| strip entries | `:132` | `expect(entries).toHaveLength(12)` | **RED** |
| tabpanel divs | `:187` | `expect(matches).toHaveLength(11)` | **RED** if the entry gets its own panel |
| `panelTargets.size` | `:219` | `expect(panelTargets.size).toBe(11)` | **PASSES FALSELY** - the `keys` array at `:203-216` is the test's OWN hardcoded list, not read from source, so it stays at 12 keys / 11 targets no matter what the strip does |
| restore-guard ladder | `:158-165` | 8 values pinned inside the `v === "discussions" ... : "record";` chain | **PASSES FALSELY** - a new value not added to the ladder restores to "record" on reload and nothing is red |

The count I verified independently: `grep -c 'role="tabpanel"'` over
`RecordingTab.tsx` finds 11 occurrences (lines 632, 835, 842, 856, 866, 876, 887,
896, 900, 904, 908). This matches `:187`.

One more trap in that test nobody has hit yet: the strip regex at `:131` is
`/\["[a-z]+",\s*"[^"]+"\]/g`. A key containing a hyphen or a digit
(`"class-trends"`, `"trends2"`) **does not match**, so the count would come back
12 and pass while the strip actually has 13. Any new key must be lowercase
letters only.

### Why the panel-inside shape wins anyway

Even setting the counts aside, a new strip entry is the wrong answer to the
owner's sentence. The owner asked for trends **alongside each grading tool**,
generated by a run. A thirteenth sibling tab is a *destination you navigate to* -
the precise thing half 2 says to stop doing. The strip counts are a reason not
to, but they are the second reason, not the first.

### What the panel-inside shape costs

Nothing in `recording-split.structure.test.ts` moves, because the recommended
chunk does not touch `RecordingTab.tsx` at all. What it does touch is the line
budget (section 2's table) - and that is why the recommended chunk mounts in
`GradingResults.tsx` (84 lines of headroom, one mount serving four surfaces)
rather than in `GradingRecordingPanel.tsx` (5 lines of headroom).

## 6. owns, verify, sabotages, residuals

### Recommended chunking

**A16-1 (this chunk, recommended for immediate dispatch):** generalize the
panel's input and mount it in `GradingResults.tsx`, disclosed by default.
Reaches surfaces 1-4 (zip, canvas, livefeed, github). Touches nothing on the
avoid list. **Verified disjoint from the live work** by mechanical intersection
(command and output below).

**A16-2 (follow, after snapshot-grading's live work lands):** mount in
`SnapshotGradingPanel`, adapting `SnapshotAssessmentRow.rubricAreas`.

**A16-3 (follow, needs a data change first):** retain `rubricAreas` through
`composeGradingRowResult` so the recording-grading tool has anything to trend,
then mount.

**A16-4 (separate, own chunk):** Repo Grades, the grid adapter.

### owns for A16-1

```
src/app/components/drafted-grades/ClassTrendsPanel.tsx
src/app/components/drafted-grades/classTrends.wiring.test.ts
src/app/components/GradingResults.tsx
src/app/components/grading-results/classTrendsMount.wiring.test.ts   [NEW]
```

Not in owns, and each named with the reason:

- `DraftedGradesTab.tsx` - **does not change** under the fan-out recommendation.
  It changes only if the owner overrules section 4, or if the prop rename forces
  the call site. **If the prop is renamed, `DraftedGradesTab.tsx:627` IS in
  owns** - it is the file that CALLS the changed export, and omitting it ships a
  type error that only `tsc` sees.
- `classTrendsDraft.not-postable.test.ts` - its canary-3 roots at `:213-218` are a
  **hardcoded four-file list**. A16-1 adds no new layer-C file, so it does not
  move. It DOES move the moment a chunk adds a new panel component; see
  RES-A16-3.
- `src/lib/grade/class-trends.ts` and the three lib modules - **untouched**.
  A16 is placement and disclosure, not computation. Anything that needs to
  change there belongs to N13b.

### Disjointness, computed not eyeballed

```bash
# A16-1 owns x the avoid list (live work). Empty is the only pass.
cat a16.txt avoid.txt | sort | uniq -d
```
Output: *(empty)*

```bash
# A16-1 owns x N13b's file set. Empty is the only pass.
cat a16.txt n13b.txt | sort | uniq -d
```
Output:
```
src/app/components/drafted-grades/ClassTrendsPanel.tsx

```

Canary for the instrument (a planted duplicate must print):
`cat a16.txt a16.txt | sort | uniq -d` printed all five paths. Canary for
absence: `grep -c "src/does-not-exist.ts" a16.txt` printed `0`.

**Conclusion: A16-1 may run concurrently with the snapshot-grading /
assessment-shared / prompts.ts live work. A16 and N13b MUST BE SEQUENCED.**
They share two files and, worse, N13b redefines `AreaTrend` to carry per-student
attribution - a fact A16's panel would be designing against while N13b
establishes it. That is informational coupling, which no file check catches.

| V7 | Whole suite | `npm test` | `Test Files`/`Tests` totals fall below the pre-change baseline, or exit non-zero |

**Single-path rule.** V1-V5 each name ONE path. Do not run them as a multi-path
vitest invocation: L14 measured that a multi-path run silently drops a path that
matches nothing and exits 0, and `closure-runner.ts:31` reads only the `Tests`
line. If they are batched for speed, **a human reads the collected file count**
and says so in the report.

**stripComments form (L13).** The existing `classTrends.wiring.test.ts:37-38`
uses the ANCHORED form `/^[ \t]*\/\/.*$/gm`, which is trailing-comment-blind - a
source-text assertion can match text sitting inside a trailing `// comment` and
pass falsely. **Any NEW assertion must use the CR-tolerant unanchored form**,
`/\/\/[^\r\n]*/g`. Repo precedent for unanchored exists at
`src/app/actions/carry-module-pattern.test.ts:639` and
`src/app/components/content-tab/modules/currentEventsAssignments.wiring.test.ts:242`.
**Caveat I am flagging rather than deciding:** unanchored stripping also eats
the `//` in any `http://` literal, so the implementer must confirm no assertion
in the file depends on a URL before converting the existing helper. If it does,
add the new helper alongside rather than converting.

**L15.** None of V1-V5 is a whole-tree walker, so none inherits the 5s-default
flake. V6's `file-size-ceiling.structure.test.ts` IS a whole-`src/` walker and
can flake red under concurrent load; a red there is re-run before it is believed.

### Sabotages - each names the file that goes red, both directions

Procedure for every row: (1) run the named test, record PASS and the counts;
(2) apply the mutation to the IMPLEMENTATION (never the test); (3) re-run, record
FAIL and which assertion; (4) restore **from a `cp` backup, never
`git checkout --`** (an uncommitted chunk's work is destroyed by a checkout);
(5) re-run, record PASS and the same counts as step 1.

| # | Mutation (implementation only) | File that goes RED |
|---|---|---|
| S1 | Delete the `<ClassTrendsPanel .../>` line from `GradingResults.tsx` | `src/app/components/grading-results/classTrendsMount.wiring.test.ts` |
| S2 | Keep the mount but pass no run-bearing prop (`<ClassTrendsPanel />`) | same file |

**S6 is not decoration.** `GradingResults.tsx` has 84 lines of headroom and this

knows the wall is real and where it is.

**S3 is the one I most expect to be skipped and it is the one that matters**,
because it is the only assertion standing between "trends renders" and "trends
renders only after a paid model call succeeds".

## 7. N13b: carried, followed, or ignored?

**FOLLOWED. A16 ships first; N13b builds on the placement A16 establishes.**

The case for carrying it is real and I want it on the record because the brief
raised it: N13b is what makes a per-run trend worth reading. Measured, from
`class-trends.ts:184-205`: `classifyDirection` reads "consistently" literally -
**every** percent value must be at or above 70, or every one at or below 60.
Four of nine students missing the same area classifies as `"mixed"` and renders a
sentence saying scores were mixed. A16 could therefore succeed completely at
placement and disclosure and put a panel in front of the instructor that says
almost nothing - which is the owner's own complaint in N13b's note.

**It is still the wrong thing to carry, for three reasons:**

1. **They are not disjoint and the coupling is informational, not just
   file-level.** N13b changes `AreaTrend` to carry per-student attribution (its
   note: "AreaTrend carries percentValues as an ANONYMOUS number[]", so
   attribution "must say exactly where attribution enters"). A16 would be
   designing a panel against a type N13b is concurrently redefining. That is
   exactly `parallel-disjointness.md` section 3's coupling, and the resolution
   there is *sequence*, not merge.

2. **N13b has an unshipped privacy constraint that A16 must not inherit
   accidentally.** Its note requires an oracle that FAILS if a student name can
   reach the class-addressed text. Merging that into a placement chunk buries a
   privacy oracle inside a chunk whose verify is about mount sites.

3. **Sequencing costs the owner nothing they can see.** A16-1's panel reads
   whatever `computeClassTrends` returns. When N13b lands, every mount A16
   created shows the richer signal with no further placement work. The reverse
   order - N13b first - leaves the richer signal reachable from one place, which
   is the situation the owner just called out.

**N13a: IGNORED by A16, and this is a real interaction to name.** N13a removes
`DEFAULT_CLASS_TRENDS_DRAFT_FLOOR = 5` (`class-trends-draft.ts:18`, enforced at
`:154`). A16's new mounts will show the "A draft needs at least 5 graded
submissions" message (`ClassTrendsDraftPanel.tsx:76-79`) more often, on more
surfaces, until N13a lands. That is a cosmetic consequence, not a blocker, and
A16 must not "fix" it by touching the floor - that is N13a's file and N13a's
decision.

## 8. What contradicts the row, my brief, or this repo's own cards

Listed because I was asked to, and because two of these would have shipped into
an implementer brief unchallenged.

1. **`class-trends-draft.ts` is 228 lines, not 214.** Both the A16 backlog row's
   `instrument` field and my brief say 214. `@(Get-Content src/lib/grade/class-trends-draft.ts).Count`
   returns **228**. Neither number is load-bearing, but the row's instrument
   field should be corrected rather than re-cited.

2. **`this-repo.md` says `GradingRecordingPanel.tsx` is 964. It is 995.**
   `@(Get-Content src/app/components/grading-recording/GradingRecordingPanel.tsx).Count`.
   That is a 5-line headroom file being described as a 36-line headroom file,
   and it is the file a "panel inside each grading tool" reading would have
   edited first.

3. **"The tools tab" framing is slightly off, and the correction matters.**
   Trends already lives in the Tools tab (`tab-sections.ts:40`, `manual: "Tools"`).
   It is one rail chip away from the grading tools, not one tab away. The owner's
   ask is about adjacency within a tab, not relocation between tabs. Anyone
   briefed as "move it into the Tools tab" will build the wrong thing.

4. **The brief's "THE TOOLS TAB IS RecordingTab.tsx" is too narrow.** RecordingTab
   is the **Recording** chip, one of ten (`tab-rails.ts:132-149`). Four other
   grading surfaces live under other chips of the same tab. Scoping A16 to the
   Recording strip would have missed the four surfaces that are easiest to serve
   and have the data to serve.

5. **The brief lists "the Live Feed / Canvas path in GradingTab.tsx, repo grades,
   and the assignment-upload tool" as three surfaces.** Live Feed, Canvas,
   assignment-upload (zip) and github are **four MODES of one component**
   (`type GradingMode = "zip" | "canvas" | "livefeed" | "github"`,
   `GradingTab.tsx:26`), three of which render the SAME `GradingResults.tsx`.
   Repo Grades is genuinely separate. This is the finding that shrinks the chunk
   from "five mounts" to "one mount plus two follow-ups".

6. **The row's framing "this is a PLACEMENT AND TRIGGER change over shipped
   logic, not a new feature" is CONFIRMED for four of the nine in-scope surfaces
   and REFUTED for one.** Surfaces 1-4 need no logic change at all. Surface 9
   (recording grading) needs a data-retention change before any placement is
   meaningful (F1). So the framing is right about the chunk I recommend and wrong
   about the tool the owner is most likely picturing when they say "the grading
   tools in the tools tab", since that is the Recording strip.

7. **I could not determine, and did not guess:** whether the owner means a series
   of assignments or a series of students (section 2, half 2). The two readings
   produce different chunks - one is a 60-line diff, the other needs a
   cross-run accumulator that does not exist. **Batched question, not a gate:**

   > When you said "run a tool over a series of assignments" - did you mean one
   > grading pass over a batch of student submissions for one assignment (which
   > is what every tool does today, and which I can ship now), or trends that
   > span several different assignments (which only the unattended workflow path
   > can produce today)? I am building the first; if you meant the second, tell
   > me and it becomes its own chunk.

   A16-1 is correct under **both** readings - it puts trends in front of a run's
   results, which the owner asked for either way - so the question rides
   alongside the work rather than blocking it.

8. **What this environment cannot verify at all, restated so nobody fills it in:**
   no rendered component, so every appearance claim is a reading claim
   (RES-A16-4); no `.env`, so layer B's route cannot be exercised end to end; no
   live model, so no claim about what the AI reading actually says. I ran no
   `npx tsc --noEmit` (an implementer owns that caller today) and made no edit to
   any file except this one.
